'''Elena Conti''' (born 14 February 1967 in [[Varese]], Italy) is an Italian biochemist and molecular biologist. She serves as Director and Scientific Member of the [[Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry]] in [[Martinsried]], Germany, where she uses [[structural biology]] and [[Biophysics|biophysical]] techniques to study [[RNA]] transport and RNA [[metabolism]].<ref name=planck>{{cite web|title=Conti, Elena|url=https://www.mpg.de/405275/biochemie_wissM90|website=www.mpg.de|language=en}}</ref>  Together with [[Elisa Izaurralde]], she helped characterize proteins important for exporting [[Messenger RNA|mRNA]] out of the [[Cell nucleus|nucleus]].<ref name=leibniz>{{cite web|title=DFG, German Research Foundation – Honour, Prize Money and "Idyllic Freedom": 2008 Leibniz Prizewinners Announced|url=https://www.dfg.de/en/service/press/press_releases/2007/pressemitteilung_nr_81/index.html|website=www.dfg.de|language=en|access-date=4 June 2020|archive-date=24 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130624180855/https://www.dfg.de/en/service/press/press_releases/2007/pressemitteilung_nr_81/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
After graduating in [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Pavia]] in 1991, Conti achieved a PhD on [[protein crystallography]] at the [[Imperial College London|Imperial College]] in London in 1996, with a thesis on the crystal structure of [[firefly luciferase]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Conti_Elena_D.pdf|title=CV|website=Leopoldina}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.biochem.mpg.de/4884771/cv|title=Curriculum Vitae|website=www.biochem.mpg.de|access-date=7 March 2019|archive-date=8 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190308080845/https://www.biochem.mpg.de/4884771/cv|url-status=dead}}</ref> From 1997 to 1999 she worked as a postdoctoral fellow at the [[Rockefeller University]] in New York City; her postdoc advisor was [[John Kuriyan]].<ref name=":0" />

==Career==
She worked as a group leader at the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory]] in [[Heidelberg]], Germany from 1999 until January 2006,<ref name=":0" /> when she became director and scientific member at the [[Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry]] in [[Martinsried]], Germany as a part of Structural Cell Biology department.<ref name="planck" /> Her research focuses on the regulation of gene expression in eukaryotic cells, particularly trying to discover the mechanism behind RNA recognition, metabolism and degradation, which is coupled to the translation machinery.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Research|url=https://www.biochem.mpg.de/conti/research|access-date=10 November 2020|website=www.biochem.mpg.de|language=en}}</ref>

She is also an honorary professor at [[LMU Munich]] in Germany since 2007.

==Awards and honors==
In 2008, Conti was awarded the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]], the most prestigious prize awarded to the researchers in Germany. The prize was shared with [[Elisa Izaurralde]] and awarded for "fundamental new insights into intracellular RNA transport and RNA metabolism."<ref name=leibniz /> In 2014 she received the [[Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine]]<ref>[https://www.jeantet.ch/en/prix-louis-jeantet/laureats/2018-en/elena-conti/ Louis-Jeantet Prize]</ref> for her important contributions to understanding the mechanisms governing RNA quality, transport and degradation. In 2018, she received the Bijvoet Medal of the [[Bijvoet Center for Biomolecular Research]] of [[Utrecht University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bijvoet-center.eu/bijvoet-medal/|title=Bijvoet Medal|publisher=Bijvoet Center for Biomolecular Research|accessdate=24 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170912191415/http://bijvoet-center.eu/bijvoet-medal/|archive-date=12 September 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> She is an elected member of [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] and of the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.embo.org/news/press-releases/2008/new-embo-members-2008|title=New EMBO Members 2008|website=EMBO|language=en-gb|access-date=7 March 2019|archive-date=8 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190308081047/http://www.embo.org/news/press-releases/2008/new-embo-members-2008|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitglieder/mitgliederverzeichnis/member/1365/|title=Mitgliederverzeichnis|website=www.leopoldina.org|language=de|access-date=7 March 2019}}</ref>
